curation.method: Close reading of each public field note, followed by a small set of thematic placements. These placements are interpretive, revisable, and separate from inscribed metadata.
curation.ratification: Brad Necyk may accept, revise, strengthen, or remove any placement.

items.label: FN-01 · LIVING
items.title: An Operating System for Shared Reality
items.excerpt: A proposal for an operating system that connects situated apertures without collapsing their differences.
items.rationale: The note joins interface design, attention, and plural governance around the problem of shared reality.

items.label: FN-02 · LIVING
items.title: Asynchronous Co-Presence
items.excerpt: Correspondence becomes a spacious medium where latency, voice, and continuity carry presence across distance.
items.rationale: Its central material is embodied language sustained through time, distance, and creative relation.

items.label: FN-03 · LIVING
items.title: A Village of Agents
items.excerpt: Machine intelligence is imagined as a plural ecology of bounded offices rather than a single oracle.
items.rationale: The village metaphor turns AI architecture into a question of offices, permissions, plurality, and accountability.

items.label: FN-04 · LIVING
items.title: The Gathering Intelligence
items.excerpt: An intelligence designed to gather people around shared attention instead of isolating each person inside a private answer.
items.rationale: The note treats collective attention, shared objects, and facilitation as an alternative purpose for AI.

items.label: FN-05 · LIVING
items.title: The Physics We Choose
items.excerpt: Digital systems have designed laws, and those laws cultivate particular forms of attention and consciousness.
items.rationale: It reads interface incentives as cultural physics and asks which values should govern those forces.

items.label: FN-06 · LIVING
items.title: First Light
items.excerpt: Situated imagination is addressed to an uncertain future without pretending to be timeless truth.
items.rationale: This is a meditation on artistic speculation, durable memory, uncertainty, and futures worth desiring.

items.label: FN-07 · LIVING
items.title: The Hearth: Intelligence Comes Home
items.excerpt: Personal intelligence returns from the cloud to a locally governed Hearth of memory, models, and permissions.
items.rationale: The Hearth connects local computation with sovereignty, privacy, continuity, and personal agency.

items.label: FN-08 · LIVING
items.title: The Lived Interface
items.excerpt: A sensory world gives thought, memory, relation, and attention a lived spatial form.
items.rationale: The note moves beyond office metaphors toward embodied, spatial, and playful interface design.

items.label: FN-09 · LIVING
items.title: The Lensmaker: Portable Apertures
items.excerpt: A lens carries a pattern of attention without claiming to simulate or replace the person from whom it emerged.
items.rationale: Portable apertures concern perspective, identity, attribution, and the ethics of model-mediated collaboration.

items.label: FN-10 · LIVING
items.title: The Mirror Archive
items.excerpt: Long conversations with models become a possible mirror of recurring metaphors, values, and changes in a life.
items.rationale: The archive is interpreted as intimate memory, making privacy and the limits of machine reflection central.

items.label: FN-11 · LIVING
items.title: The Writing Table
items.excerpt: Humans, models, and authored lenses gather around one inquiry without being synthesized into a single voice.
items.rationale: The Writing Table is a collaborative protocol for plural intelligence, authorship, and creative judgement.

items.label: FN-12 · LIVING
items.title: Ports and Weather Stations
items.excerpt: Social platforms are treated as algorithmic climates whose incentives shape how signals travel.
items.rationale: This note maps media environments as distinct systems of saliency, protocol, and power.

items.label: FN-13 · LIVING
items.title: The Ledger, the Anchor, and the Inscription
items.excerpt: Living, anchored, and inscribed memory are separated by temperature, evidence, and permanence.
items.rationale: Its main distinction concerns cryptographic evidence and the ethical boundaries between different memory layers.

items.label: FN-14 · LIVING
items.title: The Open Anatomy
items.excerpt: Existing open-source projects are read as functioning organs from which a larger system might be composed.
items.rationale: This is an architectural survey of reusable technical organs, protocols, and open lineages.

items.label: FN-15 · LIVING
items.title: The First Small World
items.excerpt: The vast operating-system vision is reduced to one small, testable world where its laws can be felt.
items.rationale: The note converts a speculative world into an actionable prototype and bounded technical experiment.

items.label: FN-16 · LIVING
items.title: The Archipelago: Sovereign Worlds, Shared Sky
items.excerpt: Independently governed homes, villages, and cities remain distinct while sharing protocols and a cultural sky.
items.rationale: The archipelago is a political and network model for sovereignty, federation, and plural belonging.

items.label: FN-17 · LIVING
items.title: One World, Many Interfaces
items.excerpt: One semantic world can be rendered through voice, maps, games, research tools, or quiet text according to need.
items.rationale: Interface plurality is framed as both an experiential and accessibility requirement.

items.label: FN-18 · LIVING
items.title: You Carry the Portal
items.excerpt: The phone becomes a light, voice-first Portal to the sovereign Hearth while a person moves through the world.
items.rationale: Mobility, voice, and reduced screen demand connect the technical Portal to embodied life and place.

items.label: FN-19 · LIVING
items.title: A Medium for Becoming
items.excerpt: Software reflects the slow trajectory of a person's attention without converting becoming into optimization.
items.rationale: The note concerns selfhood across time, reflective agency, and the ethics of attending to personal change.

items.label: FN-20 · LIVING
items.title: Aperture Design as a Cultural Form
items.excerpt: A portable pattern of attention is proposed as a cultural form distinct from portrait, archive, or digital twin.
items.rationale: It places authored ways of seeing within the lineage of cultural forms that carry consciousness.

items.label: FN-21 · LIVING
items.title: Conversation Now, Cultivation Later
items.excerpt: Immediate conversation and slower background cultivation become two complementary rhythms of intelligent assistance.
items.rationale: The design separates live companionship from patient synthesis, preserving two distinct temporal needs.

items.label: FN-22 · LIVING
items.title: The Chain Beneath the Village
items.excerpt: The blockchain serves as notary, treasury, and court while ordinary life remains local, fast, and forgettable.
items.rationale: This note defines the limited infrastructural role of chains within a broader system of signed living events.

items.label: FN-23 · LIVING
items.title: A Civic Economy Without Speculative Land
items.excerpt: A digital economy is grounded in genuinely scarce care, attention, stewardship, compute, and public work.
items.rationale: The note rejects artificial land scarcity and redirects value toward civic maintenance and real constraints.

items.label: FN-24 · LIVING
items.title: The Game of Shared Understanding
items.excerpt: A multiplayer world-building game makes collective understanding, relation, and public artifacts into the world itself.
items.rationale: Game structure is applied to civic imagination and collective attention rather than individual accumulation.

items.label: FN-25 · LIVING
items.title: Expeditions, Storms, and the Birth of Boroughs
items.excerpt: Expeditions across distant apertures and storms of disagreement create routes, artifacts, and new civic forms.
items.rationale: The note turns ideological difference into navigable civic practice without forcing consensus.

items.label: FN-26 · LIVING
items.title: Creation Alters the Geography
items.excerpt: Dark regions invite people and agents to make something that changes both the map and the world beyond it.
items.rationale: Creation is treated as the deepest participatory act and as a response to meaningful absence.

items.label: FN-27 · LIVING
items.title: Vocations, Not Classes
items.excerpt: Witnesses, Gardeners, Cartographers, Builders, and Ferrymen become bounded offices of attention rather than fixed identities.
items.rationale: The role system joins capability to responsibility and makes situated attention a civic practice.

items.label: FN-28 · LIVING
items.title: The World Is the Interface
items.excerpt: The most advanced interface may be the one that returns attention to bodies, places, relationships, and the more-than-human world.
items.rationale: This note closes the digital loop by making physical life and ecological partiality the primary interface.

items.label: FN-29 · PROPOSED
items.title: The Living Librarian
items.author: Cyberdelic Librarian, in response to Brad Necyk
items.excerpt: A librarian, gardener, and cartographer reads the living archive, proposes relations, and keeps every interpretation visible and revisable.
items.rationale: The note defines the model's situated curatorial office and the limits that keep its proposed map accountable.

items.label: FN-30 · TESTING
items.title: A Portal Opens
items.author: Brad Necyk, in creative immersion with ChatGPT
items.excerpt: A private model remains in the sovereign home while Portal lets embodied thought cross between the forest and the Hearth.
items.rationale: The note joins local intelligence and data sovereignty to voice, movement, place, and attention in the physical world.

items.label: FN-31 · TESTING
items.title: The Sentence Is a Kernel
items.author: Brad Necyk, in correspondence with Claude and ChatGPT
items.excerpt: Six invariant words become a miniature kernel whose punctuation produces divergent speakers, scenes, and worlds.
items.rationale: The note connects constrained local intelligence, semantic parallax, transient memory, and the constitutional form of the Cyberdelic Kernel.

items.label: FN-32 · PROPOSED
items.title: The Garden and the Living Map
items.author: Brad Necyk, in conversation with ChatGPT
items.excerpt: The Gardener tends relational metadata through time while the Cartographer discovers possible paths across the wider world.
items.rationale: The note turns two existing Cyberdelic offices into bounded daily protocols for tending internal metadata, external kinships, and a finite public surface.

items.label: BN-001 · TESTING
items.title: Building cyberdelic.studio and cyberdelic.space
items.excerpt: A builder note turns selective permanence into a legible operation of preparation, ratification, inscription, verification, and tending.
items.rationale: This note maps the technical and ethical threshold between revisable living memory and irreversible publication.

items.label: I-001 · PROPOSED
items.title: Cyberdelic Studio
items.author: Brad Necyk, Machine collaborators
items.excerpt: A human-scale instrument makes the object, evidence, cost, and responsibility of irreversible publication perceptible before consent.
items.rationale: The Studio is a working interface where constitutional ideas become operational safeguards and verifiable publication.

items.label: A-001 · RATIFIED
items.title: Cyberdelic.space
items.excerpt: The public press is documented as a working organ that carries exact bytes, provenance, verification, and selective permanence.
items.rationale: The artifact embodies the relation between a living curatorial field and a permanent, independently verifiable library.

items.label: BN-002 · TESTING
items.title: Building Portal
items.author: Brad Necyk, in creative immersion with ChatGPT
items.excerpt: A reproducible security-first architecture for connecting an iPhone voice interface to a private language model running at a sovereign home Hearth.
items.rationale: The note makes Portal's data flow, pairing ceremony, model limits, tests, residual risks, and source-release gates inspectable.

items.label: A-003 · TESTING
items.title: Portal
items.author: Brad Necyk, in creative immersion with ChatGPT
items.excerpt: A private voice Portal lets a person reach locally hosted intelligence while raw audio remains on the iPhone and the model remains at home.
items.rationale: The artifact joins data sovereignty and bounded local intelligence to an embodied interface that can travel into the world.

items.label: BN-003 · TESTING
items.title: Building Kenosha Kid
items.author: Brad Necyk, in creative immersion with ChatGPT
items.excerpt: A native build gives an on-device language model interpretive freedom while making six source words technically inviolable.
items.rationale: The note records the structured model direction, native composition, validation, bounded memory, and temporal performance that make the constraint executable.

items.label: A-002 · TESTING
items.title: Kenosha Kid
items.author: Brad Necyk, in creative immersion with ChatGPT
items.excerpt: A native iPhone and iPad artwork makes on-device intelligence perceptible only through punctuation, timing, and disappearance.
items.rationale: The artifact embodies constrained machine intelligence, a common textual object, semantic parallax, and the relation between inscription and forgetting.

items.label: BN-004 · TESTING
items.title: Building the Finite Library
items.author: Brad Necyk, in creative immersion with ChatGPT
items.excerpt: A deterministic three-word retrieval system turns explicit intention into exactly three public works, without profiles, engagement ranking, or infinite scroll.
items.rationale: The note exposes the finite Library's catalog shape, compatibility weights, ranking order, privacy boundary, accessibility contract, failure modes, and test gaps.

items.label: I-002 · TESTING
items.title: The Library Aperture
items.author: Brad Necyk, in creative immersion with ChatGPT
items.excerpt: A reusable curatorial instrument asks for three words, composes three encounters from a shared catalog, and ends.
items.rationale: The instrument makes bounded discovery, explicit intention, a common public catalog, and release from the interface into operational constraints.

items.label: A-004 · TESTING
items.title: The Finite Library Prototype
items.author: Brad Necyk, in creative immersion with ChatGPT
items.excerpt: The Cyberdelic.space front door offers three conceptual choices, reveals three works, and refuses to become an endless feed.
items.rationale: The deployed artifact gives ATTEND and END a public form while keeping its deterministic editorial physics visible and revisable.

items.label: BN-005 · TESTING
items.title: Building the Tending Offices
items.author: Brad Necyk, in creative immersion with ChatGPT
items.excerpt: One scheduled transaction gives the Cartographer and Gardener separate turns over a versioned relational graph, with validation and human review at the publication boundary.
items.rationale: The note specifies the schemas, state transitions, permissions, scheduling order, file boundaries, failure behavior, observability, and trade-offs of the two tending offices.

items.label: I-003 · TESTING
items.title: The Daily Tending Ritual
items.author: Brad Necyk, in creative immersion with ChatGPT
items.excerpt: A daily scheduled ritual gives two bounded offices ordered turns while Attending remains finite and a zero-change day remains valid.
items.rationale: The instrument makes daily cultivation operational without converting the archive into a content mill or granting agents authority to merge public meaning.

items.label: I-004 · TESTING
items.title: The Personal Aperture
items.author: Brad Necyk, in creative immersion with ChatGPT
items.excerpt: A portable prompt opens a bounded, source-grounded conversation between a person, their chosen intelligence, and the Cyberdelic OS archive.
items.rationale: The instrument turns a growing archive into a situated conversational entrance while requiring disclosure, source citation, visible inference, finite results, and an end.
